chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with them) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris both said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Ash'ari, who said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Hassan, from Isma'il ibn Abu Ziyad al-Sha'iri, from Thawr ibn Yazid, from Khalid ibn Sa'dan, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Knowledge had precedence, the Pen dried up, and the Divine Decree proceeded with the confirmation of the Book and the verification of the Messengers. And with happiness from Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, for whoever believed and feared Him, and with misery for whoever lied and disbelieved, and with the guardianship of Allah for the believers and His immunity from the polytheists.

Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: I transmit my tradition from Allah, indeed Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: O son of Adam! By My Will you are, and you are the one who wills for yourself what you will. By My Intent you are, and you are the one who intends for yourself what you intend. And by the favor of My grace upon you, you have strength for My disobedience. And by My protection, My help, and My health, you have fulfilled My obligations for Me.

So I am worthier of your good deeds than you are, and you are worthier of your evil deeds than I am. The good comes from Me to you as a gift from the beginning, and the evil comes from Me to you as a recompense for what you earned. And by My goodness to you, you have strength for My obedience. And by your bad opinion of Me, you have despaired of My mercy.

So the praise and the argument are Mine against you through clear explanation. And the way is Mine over you through disobedience. And for you is the reward of good with Me through goodness. I did not neglect warning you, nor did I seize you at your honor, nor did I burden you beyond your capacity, nor did I impose upon you from the trust except what you confirmed upon yourself. I am pleased with Myself for you as you are pleased with yourself for Me.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between Divine Decree and human free will in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Tawhid articulates the Shia doctrine of 'Amr bayn al-Amrayn' (the matter between the two matters), reconciling divine predestination with human free will by distinguishing between God's creative power (Qudra) and His legislative will (Irada). It emphasizes that while God provides the capacity and strength for obedience, humans are the primary agents of their choices, making them more deserving of the reward for good deeds and the burden for sins. This nuanced view underscores divine justice, asserting that God does not compel sin but grants the ability to choose, thereby establishing a clear basis for moral accountability.
